title: Strict-localization base change for an ind-etale affine map
statement:
Let $A\to B$ and $A\to C$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings, with $B$ ind-etale over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Put $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Xi\to Y$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and denote its projections by $\bar b$, $\bar c$ and their common image in $\operatorname{Spec}A$ by $\bar a$. For strict localizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], the functorial morphisms [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality] induce a canonical isomorphism
$$Y_{(\bar y)}\longrightarrow (\operatorname{Spec}B)_{(\bar b)}\times_{(\operatorname{Spec}A)_{(\bar a)}}(\operatorname{Spec}C)_{(\bar c)}.$$
Its composites with both projections are the functorial maps of strict localizations; in particular it commutes with the structural maps to $Y$. No finiteness condition on $A\to C$ and no algebraicity condition on $\Xi$ over any of the image residue fields is required.

source.place: Tag 0GIP, lemma-base-change-strict-henselization-quasi-finite, case (2), specialized to a filtered colimit of etale algebras; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0GJS, lemma-locally-acyclic-quasi-finite-base-change, displayed strict-local ring comparison

proof.text: Put $D=B\otimes_A C$. The affine fibre-product lemma identifies $Y$ with $\operatorname{Spec}D$, with its projections induced by the tensor inclusions. Write $H_A,H_B,H_C,H_D$ for the strict-localization coordinate rings at the four geometric points, all pointed into the same algebraically closed field $\Xi$. Functoriality gives local ring homomorphisms $h:H_A\to H_B$, $k:H_A\to H_C$, $l:H_B\to H_D$, and $m:H_C\to H_D$, compatible with the original structural maps. They satisfy $lh=mk$: both composites are local maps associated to the same morphism $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, and induce the same inclusion of relative separable closures inside $\Xi$; the uniqueness clause of functoriality makes them equal. Thus the canonical comparison $c:Y_{(\bar y)}\to (\operatorname{Spec}B)_{(\bar b)}\times_{(\operatorname{Spec}A)_{(\bar a)}}(\operatorname{Spec}C)_{(\bar c)}$ is the pair $(\operatorname{Spec}l,\operatorname{Spec}m)$.

source.place: Tag 0GIP, lemma-base-change-strict-henselization-quasi-finite, opening commutative square; Schemes Tag 01I4 and Algebra Tag 04GU

proof.text: Apply the affine-chart ind-etaleness statement with the whole affine schemes as charts (identity open immersions and the defining spectrum identifications). It makes $A\to H_A$, $B\to H_B$, $C\to H_C$, and $D\to H_D$ ind-etale. Composition with the given ind-etale map $A\to B$ makes $H_B$ ind-etale over $A$. Hence $h$, which is an $A$-algebra map between the ind-etale $A$-algebras $H_A,H_B$, is ind-etale by the relative-map clause of ind-etale stability. Base change makes $C\to D$ ind-etale; composing with $D\to H_D$ makes $H_D$ ind-etale over $C$. The same relative-map clause, now for $H_C,H_D$ over $C$, makes $m$ ind-etale. In particular both $h$ and $m$ are weakly etale. No assertion of ind-etaleness is needed for $A\to C$, $k$, or $l$.

source.place: Tag 04HX, lemma-describe-etale-local-ring, affine pointed-neighbourhood presentation; ind-etale stability and relative-map clause

proof.text: Functoriality states that all four $H$ rings are strictly henselian local and that $h,m$ are local ring homomorphisms. Apply the weakly etale strict-local theorem first to $h:H_A\to H_B$ and then to $m:H_C\to H_D$, using the weak etaleness proved in step 2. Each map is a ring isomorphism. Thus $u=\operatorname{Spec}h:(\operatorname{Spec}B)_{(\bar b)}\to(\operatorname{Spec}A)_{(\bar a)}$ and $z=\operatorname{Spec}m:Y_{(\bar y)}\to(\operatorname{Spec}C)_{(\bar c)}$ are isomorphisms.

Let $T=(\operatorname{Spec}B)_{(\bar b)}\times_{(\operatorname{Spec}A)_{(\bar a)}}(\operatorname{Spec}C)_{(\bar c)}$ and let $p_B,p_C$ be its projections. Since $u$ is an isomorphism, $p_C$ has inverse $s=(u^{-1}\circ\operatorname{Spec}k,\mathrm{id})$ by the fibre-product universal property. Indeed $p_Cs=\mathrm{id}$, and $sp_C=\mathrm{id}$ because its second projection is $p_C$ and its first is $u^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}k)p_C=p_B$, using the pullback equation $up_B=(\operatorname{Spec}k)p_C$. The canonical comparison from step 1 satisfies $p_Cc=z$. Therefore $c=sz$ and its inverse is $z^{-1}p_C$. Its first and second projections are exactly $\operatorname{Spec}l$ and $\operatorname{Spec}m$. Composing these with the structural maps to $\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $\operatorname{Spec}C$ gives the two projections of the strict-localization structural map to $Y$, by functoriality. The universal property of the original fibre product then gives compatibility with the structural map to $Y$. All uses of $\Xi$ concerned pointings and inclusions of relative separable closures, so no algebraicity hypothesis on $\Xi$ or finiteness hypothesis on $A\to C$ has entered.
